articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Alangium chinense (Lour.) Harms (AC) is a traditional Miao medicinal plant widely used to treat rheumatic and inflammatory disorders. Despite its therapeutic benefits, AC exhibits hepatotoxicity, limiting its safe clinical application. Traditional processing with licorice and milk has been historically employed to reduce toxicity and enhance efficacy, yet its chemical basis and underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to elucidate how licorice-milk processing alters the chemical composition of AC, identify key blood-absorbed constituents, and clarify the mechanisms underlying detoxification and efficacy enhancement. MATERIALS AND METHODS: AC was processed using an optimized licorice-milk decoction via a multi-index orthogonal design. Toxicological and pharmacological effects of raw (RAC) and processed AC (PAC) were evaluated in rats through serum biochemistry, histopathology, and xylene-induced ear edema assays. UPLC-MS/MS-based metabolomics and serum pharmacochemistry identified chemical and blood-absorbed constituents. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and Western blotting were employed to analyze hepatotoxicity-related targets and validate the involvement of signaling pathways. RESULTS: Processing significantly altered the chemical profile of AC, reducing total toxic alkaloids by 27.1% while increasing flavonoids and phenols by 14.8% and 50.2%, respectively. PAC significantly decreased rat serum AST, ALT, and ALP levels, mitigated hepatic tissue injury, and inhibited xylene-induced ear edema. Metabolomic analysis identified 56 differential compounds, with 16 unique to PAC. Serum pharmacochemistry revealed 175 blood-absorbed components, 27 of which were differentially associated with hepatotoxicity, including 18β-glycyrrhetinic acid, enoxolone, and anabasine. Network pharmacology highlighted the EGFR/PI3K/AKT cascade as a core network. Molecular docking and 100-ns MD simulations demonstrated that representative compounds formed thermodynamically stable complexes within the active site of the downstream kinase AKT1 (backbone RMSD ≈ 0.238 - 0.246 nm). Tissue-level Western blotting demonstrated that PAC modulated the aberrant expression of EGFR, p-PI3K/PI3K, and p-AKT/AKT induced by RAC, suggesting the potential involvement of this axis in mitigating hepatotoxicity. CONCLUSION: Licorice-milk processing of AC mitigates hepatotoxicity while preserving anti-inflammatory efficacy by modulating toxic alkaloids and protective metabolites. The attenuation of liver toxicity is closely associated with the systemic regulation of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. These findings provide dynamic biophysical insights into traditional processing and support the safe clinical application of AC.

articles.title: Wenyang Xiaozheng Decoction attenuates renal fibrosis and suppresses pyroptosis-associated signaling: insights from integrated transcriptomics and serum pharmacochemistry.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Wenyang Xiaozheng Decoction (WXD) is traditionally prescribed for chronic kidney disease based on the principle of warming yang and resolving blood stasis. However, whether its anti-fibrotic effects involve inflammation-associated pyroptosis remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the effects of WXD on renal fibrosis and associated changes in NF-κB- and pyroptosis-related signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Thirty-six male C57BL/6 mice were allocated to six groups and subjected to sham surgery or unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) with or without valsartan or graded doses of WXD. The effects of WXD were further evaluated in TGF-β1/TNF-α-stimulated HK-2 cells. Kidney transcriptomics was integrated with serum pharmacochemistry-based network pharmacology restricted to blood-absorbed constituents. Pharmacological perturbations using necrosulfonamide (NSA) and lipopolysaccharide (LPS) were performed in HK-2 cells. RESULTS: High-dose WXD reduced serum BUN, renal fibrotic area, and GSDMD-N expression by 24.7%, 27.6%, and 29.1%, respectively, compared with UUO mice (all P < 0.05). Transcriptomic analysis showed that WXD reversed UUO-induced activation of NF-κB, TNF, and NOD-like receptor signaling. Integration with serum pharmacochemistry identified 36 blood-absorbed constituents and yielded inflammation-related target and pathway profiles consistent with the transcriptomic findings. WXD reduced the abundance of phosphorylated p65, cleaved caspase-1, and GSDMD-N in vivo and in vitro. NSA partially reproduced, whereas LPS partially counteracted, the protective effects of WXD. CONCLUSIONS: WXD attenuates renal fibrosis in association with reduced NF-κB- and pyroptosis-associated signaling. Integrating transcriptomics with network pharmacology based on blood-absorbed constituents provides a biologically relevant strategy for investigating multi-component traditional Chinese medicine formulas.

articles.title: Schinifoline attenuates atherosclerosis and modulates gut microbiota and bile acid metabolism in ApoE-/- mice.
articles.abstract: Atherosclerosis (AS) remains a major global health burden despite advances in lipid-lowering therapies. Zanthoxylum bungeanum Maxim (ZBM) has demonstrated anti-atherosclerotic potential; however, the role of its active component, schinifoline (SF), in atherosclerosis remains unclear. In this study, we evaluated the anti-atherosclerotic effects of SF in high-fat diet (HFD)-fed ApoE-/- mice. SF treatment attenuated aortic plaque formation, improved serum lipid parameters, and decreased inflammatory responses. Integrated 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics revealed that high-dose SF partially restored HFD-associated alterations in gut microbiota composition, including normalization of the Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio and changes in several atherosclerosis-associated genera, and altered bile acid profiles. In addition, SF reduced intestinal apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter (ASBT) expression, suggesting a potential role in bile acid homeostasis. Collectively, these findings indicate that SF attenuates atherosclerosis and is associated with alterations in gut microbiota, bile acid profiles, and lipid and inflammatory responses, providing insights into its pharmacological effects.

articles.title: Isorhapontigenin alleviates sepsis-induced acute lung injury by targeting the RAF1-ERK1/2-CXCL10 axis to inhibit CXCR3+ neutrophil recruitment.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction syndrome resulting from a dysregulated host response to infection and is characterized by persistent hyperinflammation followed by immunosuppression. Isorhapontigenin (ISO), a natural stilbene derivative found in Chinese herbs and grapes, possesses potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its potential therapeutic role in sepsis remains unclear. In this study, we investigated the protective effects of ISO against sepsis-induced multi-organ injury and the underlying molecular mechanisms. Using a murine model of sepsis, we observed that ISO administration considerably suppressed the expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor-α in the tissues. Furthermore, ISO treatment markedly improved survival rates and attenuated pathological damage in the liver and lung. Transcriptomic profiling revealed that ISO confers protection by modulating inflammatory cascades and inhibiting chemokine-mediated immune cell migration. Notably, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 10 (CXCL10) was identified as a key hub gene. Mechanistically, ISO directly binds to RAF proto-oncogene serine/threonine-protein kinase (RAF1) and inhibits the RAF1-extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway, thereby downregulating CXCL10 expression and preventing excessive infiltration of C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 3-positive (CXCR3+) neutrophils into pulmonary tissue. In conclusion, our findings demonstrate that ISO mitigates sepsis-induced lung injury via the RAF1/ERK1/2/CXCL10 axis, providing a potential mechanistic basis for further investigation of ISO as a therapeutic candidate for sepsis.

articles.title: Translational Evaluation of In Vitro-to-In Vivo Extrapolation Techniques for Brain Penetration Using Open Flow Microperfusion and Microdialysis in Rats.
articles.abstract: There is a growing need to leverage mathematical models of the central nervous system (CNS) with translational approaches employing in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) approaches. As a benchmark of brain penetration, unbound brain partitioning (Kp,uu), and subsequently a combination of cerebral Open Flow Microperfusion (cOFM) and microdialysis (MD) were evaluated in rats. Additionally, a six-compartment physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of the CNS was developed in rats using six drugs with varying affinities to the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) transporter to learn and verify the in vivo studies. Active and passive drug efflux and permeability parameters derived from two P-gp overexpressing cell lines (MDCK-I and LLC-PK1) were scaled using proteomics-informed methods. Model predictions were evaluated with data obtained from terminal brain-to-plasma partition coefficient from both rat cOFM and MD experiments. In correcting for loss of drug in both the cOFM and MD equipment, a relative recovery (RR) showed significantly higher recovery in cOFM compared to MD experiments; for phenytoin, quinidine, and verapamil these were 0.53/0.063, 0.73/0.46, and 0.16/0.04 (cOFM/MD), respectively. Notably, higher P-gp efflux obtained from experiments with MDCK-I-transfected cells resulted in simulated lower drug concentrations in brain compartments. Overall, the CNS-IVIVE-PBPK model tended to overpredict brain drug concentrations, especially using data obtained from transfected LLC-PK1 cells. However, there is better agreement between the model predictions and the observed data for whole-brain concentrations obtained from terminal studies. We also demonstrated the feasibility of an IVIVE framework that integrates cell line derived passive and active drug parameters to estimate brain concentrations.

articles.title: Apoptotic body-liposome hybrid nanoparticles with photothermal-enhanced blood-brain barrier penetration for radiation-induced brain injury therapy.
articles.abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) is a severe brain disease caused by cranial radiotherapy or accidental radiation exposure. RIBI causes overproduction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), resulting in oxidative injury to neurons and brain tissue and promoting neuroinflammation. Current treatments such as antioxidants, have limited efficacy due to limited penetration across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and rapid metabolic clearance. This study developed Prussian blue (PB) nanoparticles encapsulated in apoptotic body-hybrid liposomes to improve BBB penetration and ensure sustained antioxidative activity through controlled release of PB. PB serve as nanozymes for sustained ROS scavenging, while their photothermal response facilitates transient BBB modulation under near-infrared irradiation. Hybridization with apoptotic bodies provides a biomimetic membrane interface that supports cellular interactions and brain delivery. 2-Methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC)-modified DSPE-PEG2000 was incorporated through choline-related transport pathways for brain-targeted delivery. In vitro, PB@AbL showed approximately 55% DPPH radical-scavenging activity. In vivo, brain drug accumulation was increased by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS). Pharmacodynamic analysis showed reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, increased glutathione (GSH) levels, improved neuronal survival, and cognitive function. This strategy offers a promising approach for the treatment of RIBI and other neurological disorders associated with oxidative stress.

articles.title: Arginine regulates intermolecular interactions to stabilize lyophilized high-concentration omalizumab: dry-state characterizations and molecular dynamics insights into reconstitution and viscosity.
articles.abstract: High-concentration monoclonal antibody formulations (HCMFs) are widely adopted in modern biopharmaceuticals owing to their suitability for subcutaneous administration and superior patient compliance. Nevertheless, lyophilized HCMFs face major technical obstacles, including high solution viscosity, prolonged reconstitution duration, and excessive bubble formation, which impair manufacturability and impede clinical translation. While arginine serves as an effective viscosity-lowering excipient for concentrated protein solutions, its low intrinsic glass transition temperature (Tg') leads to lyophilization instability and cake collapse. These drawbacks limit its applicability in freeze-dried products. In this work, a binary excipient system consisting of trehalose and low-dose arginine was developed to overcome the above limitations. The high Tg' of trehalose synergistically offsets the low-Tg'-associated deficiencies of arginine within concentrated protein matrices, thereby maintaining favorable long-term physical and chemical stability of lyophilized omalizumab. Molecular dynamics simulations of reconstituted high-concentration omalizumab solutions further revealed the underlying viscosity-reduction mechanism. Arginine attenuates attractive protein-protein interactions, enlarges the colloidal radius (Rc) of antibody assemblies, promotes water infiltration into colloidal voids, and intensifies molecular Brownian motion, which fundamentally reduces solution viscosity and improves reconstitution performance. Overall, this study clarifies the incompatibility between arginine and lyophilized omalizumab and provides mechanistic guidance for the molecular modulation of viscosity in high-concentration monoclonal antibody formulations.

articles.title: Development of dissolving polymeric microneedles loaded with benzocaine nanocrystals as an effective intradermal drug delivery system.
articles.abstract: The development of dissolving polymeric microneedles (DPMNs) loaded with drug nanocrystals is an innovative and minimally invasive approach for localized drug administration. In this work, benzocaine, a short-acting local anesthetic, was formulated into nanocrystals (BZ-NCs) and subsequently incorporated into polymeric microneedles. Several formulations of BZ-NCs were formulated via nanoprecipitation technique, utilizing ethanol as a solvent and varying aqueous concentrations of sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS), Polysorbate 80, or Poloxamer 188 as the antisolvent. The optimized formulation of BZ-NCs, which was developed utilizing 0.5% w/v SLS in the antisolvent phase, was assessed employing attenuated total reflectance-Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Moreover, the dissolution behavior of BZ-NCs was compared to that of plain benzocaine (BZ). DPMNs loaded with the optimized BZ-NCs formulation were prepared by mixing 25% w/w polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and 35% w/w polyvinyl pyrrolidone (PVP) at ratios of 1:3, 1:2, or 1:1, respectively. The favorable formulation (1:1) was selected for further evaluation, including dissolution, accelerated stability, histological assessment and dermatokinetic analysis. The optimized nanocrystal formulation (BZ-NCs-3), exhibited a particle size of 291.12 ± 15.31 nm with polydispersity index and zeta potential of 0.261 ± 0.090 and -32.27 ± 1.04, respectively. ATR-FTIR confirmed the chemical structure integrity of benzocaine in BZ-NCs-3, while PXRD and DSC revealed its crystalline nature. Moreover, the dissolution of BZ-NCs-3 was significantly enhanced at pH 5.5 and 7.4 compared to BZ. The optimal microneedle formulation (BZNCs-MN3), having the highest PVA content, demonstrated effective penetration in excised human skin reaching a depth of 394.19 ± 20.402 µm, dissolved within 25 min and showed no significant changes in benzocaine content after accelerated storage. According to the dermatokinetic analysis, delayed and superior deposition of benzocaine in the epidermis and dermis were recorded following the application of BZNCs-MN3. This platform provides promise for improving local anesthesia with higher distribution of benzocaine in skin layers.

articles.title: Effect of human skin storage on stratum corneum drug penetration assessed by confocal Raman spectroscopy.
articles.abstract: Fresh human skin is the preferred model for ex vivo dermal penetration studies. However, limited availability often necessitates frozen storage. We investigated whether storage for two months at -20 °C or -80 °C affects skin barrier function, selected Raman-derived skin properties, and drug penetration. For each of six donors, paired full-thickness abdominal skin samples were analyzed fresh or after frozen storage. Barrier integrity was assessed by transepidermal water loss, while quantitative confocal Raman spectroscopy was used to determine water concentration profiles and the amount of caffeine, diclofenac sodium, and salicylic acid within the upper 15 µm after application of 2% (w/w) hydrogels for 1 h. Transepidermal water loss varied across storage conditions, although neither frozen-storage condition differed significantly from fresh skin. Raman-derived water content was significantly higher after storage at -80 °C than in fresh or -20 °C-stored skin, whereas no consistent storage-related differences were detected in the fingerprint spectra or combined ceramide and fatty acid signal. Caffeine penetration was 18.57, 19.82, and 21.51 µg/cm2 in fresh, -20 °C-stored, and -80 °C-stored skin, respectively, with significantly greater penetration in -80 °C-stored skin than in fresh skin. No significant differences were detected for diclofenac sodium or salicylic acid. Under these conditions, storage at -20 °C did not significantly alter the Raman-derived stratum corneum parameters or drug penetration outcomes, whereas storage at -80 °C altered the superficial Raman-derived water signal and caffeine penetration. Storage conditions should therefore be standardized for each compound and experimental endpoint.

articles.title: In situ antibacterial thermosensitive hydrogel as a versatile platform for diabetic wound therapy and molecular monitoring.
articles.abstract: Chronic diabetic wounds are difficult to manage because of persistent inflammation, impaired tissue regeneration, and high infection risk under hyperglycemic conditions. Microbial colonization further aggravates inflammatory responses and disrupts the normal progression of wound healing. Here, we developed a multifunctional hydrogel composed of Pluronic F-127 (PF) and tannic acid (TA), where TA acted as a natural crosslinker to improve network stability and gelation behavior. The PF/TA hydrogel exhibited in situ thermosensitive gelation within the physiological temperature range (33-37 °C), enabling rapid solidification and strong adhesion to wound surfaces. Rheological and microscopic analyses confirmed favorable viscoelasticity and a microporous structure. The hydrogel also showed antibacterial activity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. To provide therapeutic functionality, the hydrogel was loaded with Humulus scandens (HS) or Vitis vinifera (VV) extracts. These extracts reduced Pecam1 expression, promoted fibroblast proliferation, increased Col1a1 expression, and induced M2 macrophage polarization in vitro. For wound monitoring, gold nanoparticle-based mRNA nanosensors (NanoFlares) were incorporated to detect Pecam1 and Col1a1 mRNA associated with inflammatory and proliferative healing phases. In non-infected murine wound models, HS- and VV-loaded PF/TA hydrogels significantly accelerated wound closure under both nondiabetic and diabetic conditions, demonstrating promising potential for diabetic wound therapy and monitoring applications.

articles.title: Disruption of endosomal transport in cyclodextrin-mediated cytotoxicity.
articles.abstract: Cyclodextrins (CDs) are widely used as pharmaceutical excipients, yet their systemic use is constrained by cytotoxic effects that remain incompletely understood. While β-cyclodextrins are commonly associated with cholesterol extraction, it remains unclear whether this mechanism alone explains their biological activity. Here, we investigate the effects of native and modified CDs in human renal proximal tubule cells using complementary imaging, flow cytometry, and MALDI mass spectrometry. Distinct, host-dependent responses were observed. α-Cyclodextrin induced rapid membrane disruption at elevated concentrations, whereas methylated β-cyclodextrin (Meβ-CD) produced a progressive phenotype characterized by increased membrane permeability, impaired lipid internalization, and reduced cell proliferation under sub-lethal conditions. Despite these differences, both Meβ-CD and γ-cyclodextrin enhanced cholesterol internalization without evidence of immediate depletion, indicating modulation of endogenous transport processes. In contrast, Meβ-CD selectively disrupted membrane lipid uptake and altered extracellular lipid composition, yielding vesicle fractions enriched in cholesterol esters and ceramides but depleted in phosphoinositides. These findings support a model in which cyclodextrins perturb phosphoinositide-dependent lipid trafficking pathways, providing a mechanistic link between altered lipid distribution and cytotoxic response, and informing the design of safer CD-based therapeutics.

articles.title: Development and preclinical characterization of an MMAE-conjugated anti-EpCAM antibody-drug conjugate for colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: The epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) is frequently overexpressed in colorectal cancer (CRC) and thus represents an attractive therapeutic target. However, the clinical efficacy of EpCAM-targeting antibodies has been limited by suboptimal binding properties and reliance on immune effector mechanisms. Here, we describe the development and characterization of anti-EpCAM #126, a fully human monoclonal antibody isolated from the OPAL phage-display library, and its corresponding antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). Anti-EpCAM #126 exhibited substantially higher binding affinity than adecatumumab, primarily owing to a markedly lower dissociation rate. High-density peptide microarray analysis and alanine-scanning mutagenesis identified NGSKLGRRAK (residues 74-83) within the EpCAM extracellular domain as the dominant epitope, with S76, R81, and K83 serving as key contact residues. Binding was conformation-dependent and markedly decreased following trypsin-mediated proteolytic cleavage of the epitope region. Anti-EpCAM #126 demonstrated robust staining of CRC xenograft and patient-derived tumor tissues and exhibited low cytokine release in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and mouse models. Following the confirmation of efficient receptor-mediated internalization, anti-EpCAM #126 was conjugated to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) through a protease-cleavable valine-alanine linker, generating an ADC with a controlled average drug-to-antibody ratio of 4.31 while retaining nanomolar EpCAM-binding affinity. The resulting ADC exhibited potent cytotoxicity against EpCAM-expressing CRC cell lines and achieved 84.96% tumor growth inhibition in a patient-derived xenograft model at 10 mg/kg, whereas the unconjugated antibody showed no antitumor activity. These findings suggest that anti-EpCAM #126-MMAE is a high-affinity, epitope-specific ADC with promising preclinical efficacy against EpCAM-positive CRC.

articles.title: Harnessing Functionalized Nano Lipid Carriers for Cardioprotection: Dual Drug Delivery in Focus for Precision Therapeutics.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of global mortality, accounting for approximately 17.9 million deaths worldwide in 2019, with nearly 85% caused by heart attacks and strokes. Despite significant advancements in conventional pharmacotherapy, challenges such as poor bioavailability, non-specific drug targeting, rapid degradation, and limited therapeutic efficacy continue to hinder effective cardiovascular treatment. This review aims to explore the potential of nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) as advanced drug delivery systems for cardioprotection, with special emphasis on dual drug-loaded and functionalized NLC strategies. SIGNIFICANCE OF REVIEW: NLCs, composed of blends of solid and liquid lipids, have emerged as promising nanocarriers due to their enhanced drug loading capacity, controlled release behaviour, improved drug solubility, and excellent biocompatibility. Surface functionalization of NLCs with specific targeting ligands enables site-specific delivery to cardiovascular tissues, thereby minimizing systemic toxicity and improving therapeutic outcomes. Furthermore, the incorporation of dual therapeutic agents within a single NLC platform offers synergistic cardioprotective effects and enhanced treatment efficiency. KEY FINDINGS: The review highlights recent advancements in ligand-functionalized and dual drug-loaded NLC systems for cardiovascular therapy. These nanocarriers demonstrate improved pharmacokinetic profiles, sustained drug release, enhanced tissue targeting, and reduced off-target effects. Additionally, individualized NLC-based formulations tailored to patient-specific therapeutic requirements show significant promise in precision cardiovascular medicine. CONCLUSIONS: Functionalized dual drug-loaded NLCs represent a novel and promissing strategy for improving cardioprotective therapy. Their ability to enhance targeted delivery, therapeutic efficacy, and patient safety positions them as a transformative platform for future cardiovascular disease management, pending preclinical and clinical validation.

articles.title: Polymer-based Vaginal Insert Systems: Engineering Controlled Drug Delivery for Women's Health.
articles.abstract: Polymer-based vaginal inserts have emerged as a promising approach for localized and systemic drug delivery, demonstrating improved therapeutic efficacy, prolonged drug residence, controlled release and enhanced patient compliance compared to conventional vaginal dosage forms. This article gives a complete overview of the design and development of polymer-based vaginal inserts, covering the influence of vaginal physiology, mucoadhesion and polymer selection on formulation performance. The properties and applications of natural, synthetic, and hybrid polymers, and current breakthroughs in fabrication technologies such as freeze-drying, solvent casting, hot-melt extrusion, electrospinning, and 3D printing are covered. Also examined are several drug release techniques such as sustained, swelling-controlled, stimuli-responsive and mucoadhesive systems. Moreover, the therapeutic potential of vaginal inserts for the treatment of vulvovaginal infections, endometriosis, cervical cancer, uterine fibroids, menopause-related illnesses, contraception and HIV prevention is emphasized. Finally, the future directions of emerging technologies, such as nanotechnology, smart polymers, artificial intelligence, and personalized drug delivery systems, are discussed for the clinical translation and enhanced efficacy of polymer-based vaginal drug delivery systems for women's reproductive health.

articles.title: Vilazodone Hydrochloride-Loaded Nanostructured Lipid Carrier In Situ Gel for Intranasal Nose-to-Brain Antidepressant Delivery.
articles.abstract: The Oral delivery of vilazodone hydrochloride (VLZ), a serotonin partial agonist-reuptake inhibitor for major depressive disorder, suffers from extensive hepatic first-pass metabolism, food-dependent absorption, and poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, limiting its central therapeutic impact. Here, VLZ-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (NLCs) were engineered and embedded within a Poloxamer 407/188-chitosan thermosensitive in situ gel to enable direct nose-to-brain delivery. The NLCs were fabricated by combined high-shear and high-pressure homogenisation and optimised through central composite design, yielding a batch with particle size 24.74 ± 2.23 nm, polydispersity index 0.248 ± 0.012, and entrapment efficiency 91.37 ± 4.56%. The lyophilised NLCs were incorporated into an in situ gel with a physiologically appropriate gelation temperature of 34°C and gelation time of 42 s. Fourier Transform Infrared FTIR spectroscopy confirmed complete drug encapsulation, evidenced by disappearance of the diagnostic nitrile (C≡N) absorption band, while DSC and XRPD verified conversion of VLZ to an amorphous state within the lipid matrix. Drug release followed Korsmeyer-Peppas kinetics, sustained over 24 h, and the formulation remained stable under refrigerated storage. In Swiss albino mice, the intranasal NLC-in situ gel (1 mg/kg) produced a profound antidepressant-like effect relative to oral pure drug (10 mg/kg) across open field, tail suspension, and sucrose preference tests, consistent with enhanced nose-to-brain delivery via the olfactory and trigeminal pathways. Hence this nanocarrier-hydrogel strategy offers a promising, non-invasive route to enhanced CNS delivery of antidepressants.

articles.title: Target-Engagement Prediction From Molecular Structure, In Vitro and Animal Data: A Tutorial for Early Assessment of Clinical Drug Exposure and Therapeutic/Adverse Potential Using the ANDROMEDA and PLATO Software on the InSilicoTrials Platform.
articles.abstract: The target-engagement predictor, implemented within the InSilicoTrials cloud-based, AI-powered platform for model-informed drug discovery and development, enables early exploration of time-dependent pharmacological responses. Predictions can be generated using inputs ranging from molecular structure to in vitro, animal, and clinical data. Scaling and translation across species are supported, accounting for differences in body size and plasma protein binding. This tutorial demonstrates the application of the target-engagement predictor for benchmarking and decision-support in the evaluation of new drug candidates. Pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) data for carvedilol, ivabradine, and sunitinib were used as illustrative examples. The ANDROMEDA and PLATO software were used to predict human clinical PK and target affinity parameters, respectively, based on molecular SMILES representations of the drugs. These predictions were subsequently incorporated into longitudinal PKPD simulation models. User-friendly input wizards and interactive results dashboards were developed to facilitate clinical trial simulation for broader project teams, without requiring programming expertise. Predictions derived from molecular structure were compared with data generated from in vitro, rat, and clinical experimental settings. The target-engagement predictor enables integration of heterogenous data sources to support drug development decisions, including early benefit-risk assessment and dose selection for Phase 1 studies. Direct prediction based on molecular structure alone represents a promising approach for early-stage screening and evaluation of new drug candidates.

articles.title: Development of an Injectable Boronic Ester Nanocomposite Hydrogel for pH- and Thermo-Responsive Gentamicin Delivery and Antibacterial Activity.
articles.abstract: Infected wounds require localized antimicrobial treatment strategies that provide sustained drug release, reduce systemic antibiotic exposure, and promote tissue repair. This study reports an infection-responsive nanocomposite hydrogel platform based on dynamic covalent boronic ester chemistry for triggered topical antibiotic delivery. Phenylboronic acid (PBA)-functionalized cationic nanoparticles (PBA-NPs) were employed as three-dimensional crosslinkers and combined with poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) to construct an injectable nanocomposite hydrogel via reversible boronic ester interactions. The nanocomposite hydrogel was characterized for morphology, injectability, rheological properties, stimuli-responsive behavior, in vitro antibiotic release, and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The resulting nanocomposite hydrogel exhibited a gel-sol transition at 39.7°C, while the pH-dependent chemistry of the boronic ester network supports enhanced network dissociation under mildly acidic conditions (pH 6.5). This dual pH- and thermo-responsive behavior enabled on-demand release of encapsulated gentamicin sulfate while preserving viscoelastic recovery consistent with dynamic network reconstruction. The cationic PBA-NPs exhibited intrinsic antibacterial activity and generated enhanced antimicrobial effects when combined with gentamicin. Zones of inhibition reached 22 mm (S. aureus) and 25 mm (P. aeruginosa) at 3% drug loading. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that dynamic covalent boronic ester nanocomposite hydrogel represents a promising injectable platform for infection-responsive localized antibiotic delivery and antibacterial wound management.

articles.title: From discrimination to transportability: Interpreting machine-learning prediction of antitubercular drug-induced liver injury.
